title: The concert programme
summary: Plan the order of pieces, write a spoken introduction for each, and time the whole set.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil
a card for the spoken introductions

figure.alt: Four boxes stacked, an example concert programme order. The real list may hold more or fewer pieces, each with its own spoken introduction planned in advance.

steps.title: The concert programme
steps.body:
A concert is more than pieces played one after another. It has an order, an introduction for each piece, and a total time that someone planned on purpose. All three are decisions you can make now instead of on the day.

1. List every piece for the year's concert, in the order you plan to play them.
2. Write one sentence to say before each piece: its name and one thing worth knowing about it.
3. Run through the whole programme once, pieces and spoken lines together, and time it with the phone.
4. If two similar-sounding pieces sit next to each other, move one so the programme has more variety.

Planning the order and the words in advance means the only thing left to think about on the day is the playing itself.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: list the pieces in order, write the first two introductions
Sitting 2: write the rest of the introductions
Sitting 3: run the whole programme once, pieces and words together, time it
Sitting 4: adjust the order if needed, run it again as if recording
An old piece added to the programme if there is room

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Record the full programme run-through in one take, spoken introductions included, hands in the frame.
